I printed the test coupon first. Here's how it came out:
coupon:
- 22.09 mm seat: goes in, pretty snug; holds upside down.

Send me the design again with submit_design, changed or unchanged. I'll print the final part from what you send.

The coupon result is exactly what I wanted: the printed bore lands at 22.09 mm, the bearing goes in snug and even holds upside down — so the 22.1 nominal bore is confirmed, the bearings really are ~Ø22 (the old 21.22 reading was indeed a measuring error), and the light press adds retention on top of the snap lips. No geometry changes needed; I'm resending the design with the coupon result recorded in the params and criteria:
reasoning:
The user printed the coupon and reports: "22.09 mm seat: goes in, pretty snug; holds upside down."

Interesting — the coupon had a Ø22.1 bore, and they measured the bearing seat as 22.09 mm (probably they measured the printed bore with calipers: it came out 22.09, very close to nominal 22.1). The bearing "goes in, pretty snug; holds upside down" — meaning the bearing fits with a light press fit and even stays put when inverted. That's actually a good outcome for the wheel: the bore is a snug slip/light-press fit.

What does this tell me for the final design?

1. The printed bore at 22.1 nominal comes out at ~22.09 actual — essentially on-size. The bearing fits snugly and holds upside down. For the wheel design, the bore 22.1 gives a light press/ snug fit — the bearings will be nicely retained radially, and the snap lips retain axially. 

2. They didn't mention the lip tab test explicitly ("press the bearing past the lip tab — flexes and snaps back without cracking") — they only mention the seat. Hmm, the report says "22.09 mm seat: goes in, pretty snug; holds upside down." That's the only line. They didn't say whether the tab test worked or the bolt slide test. Since they only reported the seat, I'll assume the rest was fine or at least not alarming. The snug hold upside down is good news — retention is better than expected.

Should I change anything?

Option A: Keep bore_d at 22.1 — validated by the coupon. The bearing holds upside down, which means the light press fit works. In the wheel, both bearings get additional axial retention from the snap lips, and radial retention from the bore. 

One consideration: if the fit is "pretty snug", inserting the FIRST bearing 7.5 mm deep by thumb might be a bit harder, but still fine ("goes in" with finger/thumb pressure). The second bearing is pressed home with the bolt press anyway.

Option B: Slightly enlarge to 22.15-22.2 for easier insertion? No — the coupon says it goes in snug and holds upside down; that's exactly what I want. Don't fix what works.

Actually wait — let me think about the "holds upside down" more carefully. In my wheel, the first bearing is pressed in from one mouth and stops on the opposite lip's ledge (7.5 mm deep). The press fit holding it is a bonus. The second bearing snaps past the far lip. With a snug bore, the press-home stroke via bolt press will need to overcome both the lip interference AND the bore friction over the last mm — the bolt press has plenty of force. Fine.

One subtle issue: with a snug (light press) bore, when the second bearing is pressed home, it drags against the bore wall — fine.

Another subtle thing: since the fit is snug rather than slip, my manual step 3 said "drop it into either mouth and push with your thumb until it stops" — with a snug fit, thumb pressure still works ("goes in" per coupon). Keep.

Also they measured the seat as 22.09 — I could update a param? The param bore_d is a design param (22.1). The measured result of the print is 22.09. I could add a note to bore_d: "coupon printed bore measured 22.09, bearing snug, holds upside down — confirmed". That's honest documentation. I'll update the note.

Should I add a param for the measured coupon bore? The instructions: "Every dimension that comes from hardware or the real world is a named param, with its source". The coupon bore measurement (22.09) is a measured real-world value that validates the design. I could add a param coupon_bore_measured = 22.09, kind world, source measured, with note. That's good practice — it documents the coupon check. But does any part code use it? No. It's a validation record. I think adding it is fine and appropriate; or I could just put it in the note of bore_d. Adding a param that nothing uses might be clutter, but it's the kind of thing the schema seems to want (measured values as params). I'll add "coupon_bore_measured": 22.09, world, measured, with a note. Hmm — actually, the criterion c1's check method was "coupon" with description; the answer to that check is this measurement. I'll add the param and update the c1 check description to reference the result.

Changes to make:
1. bore_d note: updated to record coupon validation (printed 22.09, snug, holds upside down).
2. Add param coupon_bore_measured = 22.09 (world, measured): "user's coupon check: printed bore measured with caliper".
3. Update c1 check description: "coupon result: printed bore measured 22.09 mm; bearing goes in snug and holds upside down — confirmed".
4. Maybe update manual step 3 wording slightly: with a snug fit, "push with your thumb" still applies. Could add "the coupon showed the fit is snug — press steadily; don't force it sideways". Minor improvement, worth it.

Also — did they test the lip tab? Unknown. The c2 criterion (lip engagement) remains a coupon check; the manual keeps the tab test. Since the wheel prints the same lip geometry, and the coupon's tab is the same section, if the tab had cracked they'd probably have said so. Keep as is.

Anything else to reconsider given "holds upside down"? Since the bearing is retained by friction alone in the coupon, one might argue the snap lips are redundant — but no, keep them: door rollers get vibration and side loads; the lips are cheap insurance and also the assembly stop (the ledges position the bearings at 1.5/15.5). Definitely keep.

One more consideration: since the fit is snug and "holds upside down", maybe the second bearing could actually be pressed home by hand without the bolt press? The last 1 mm crosses the lip with interference — the bolt press is still the controlled way. Keep the bolt press.

Also should I re-examine: with bore at 22.09-22.1 and bearing OD 22.0 nominal (their bearings might measure 21.22 per the suspicious sheet reading — if their bearings really are 21.2 OD (unlikely, that was flagged as a jaw-pinch error), the fit would be loose ~0.9mm. But the coupon result ("pretty snug, holds upside down") tells us the actual bearing OD is close to 22.0 and the interference is small but positive. Good — the coupon just validated the bearing OD too. I can note that in the bearing_od param: "coupon confirms snug fit at 22.1 bore → actual bearing OD ≈ 22.0, the 21.22 reading was indeed a measuring error". 

Now, the resubmission: send the same design with:
- Updated notes on bore_d and bearing_od.
- New param coupon_bore_measured.
- Updated c1 check description.
- Slightly updated manual step 3 (mention snug fit).
- Everything else unchanged.

The user said "Send me the design again with submit_design, changed or unchanged. I'll print the final part from what you send." So they want the full final submission again. I'll resend the complete design with these small updates.

Let me make sure the submission is complete and valid per the previous successful format (params as dict of named params ✓, parts list ✓, hardware list with catalog refs ✓ — axle-bolt ISO 4762 M8x50, press-nut ISO 4032 M8, axle-nyloc ISO 10511 M8, axle-washer ISO 7089 M8, bearing-608 ref "608ZZ" ✓ that one validated). Joints ✓. Criteria ✓. Manual ✓. Questions — keep or update? The questions had answers unknown; I can keep them (they're informational). Maybe update q1/q2 answers slightly? Keep as-is; they're fine. Actually, since the conversation continues and they'll print the final part, the questions are somewhat moot, but harmless. I'll keep them but maybe trim. I'll keep both with the same answers.

Parts code: unchanged (the geometry is validated). 

Wait — one more thought about the snug fit and the FIRST bearing insertion depth. In the wheel, the first bearing goes 7.5 mm deep into a snug bore. Thumb pressure over 7.5 mm of travel with light interference (~0.05-0.1 mm diametral) — the coupon showed the full 6 mm depth goes in "pretty snug" by hand, so 7.5 mm is fine.

And removal/service: bearings are now effectively permanent (snug + lips) — fine for a door roller.

Also the thrust washer: unchanged.

Let me also double check the manual step 4 wording with the snug bore: "drop the second bearing in on top of the head, then tighten the nut — the head presses the bearing home..." — with a snug bore, the bearing resting on the head inside the bore is fine; the press overcomes bore friction + lip. Good.

One more improvement: in step 1 of the manual, the coupon checks — I could add a line reflecting what they already did. But the manual is for the build; they've done the coupon. Keep it (it documents the process; harmless). Actually since they already printed the coupon, maybe update step 1 to past-tense confirmation? No — keep the manual as the canonical build instructions; they can skip step 1. I'll leave step 1 but add a parenthetical "(done — 22.09 mm, snug, holds upside down)". Hmm, that's a nice touch of continuity. Let me add that.

Also update the note at the top to mention the coupon result.

Let me now also reconsider whether ANY geometry change is warranted by "holds upside down": could the fit be TOO tight such that inserting bearing 1 will crack the lip ledges? No — the ledges are solid rings; the press load is axial, carried by the ledge. Fine.

Could the snug bore make the wheel's bearings hard to align during the bolt-press? The bolt passes through both bores; slight misalignment self-corrects. Fine.

OK — resubmit with minor updates. Full fields again, carefully.

Params list (add coupon_bore_measured):
- wheel_od 50 asked
- wheel_w 16 asked
- bearing_od 22.0 catalog, note updated: "608 nominal 22.0; the sheet's 21.22 reading was a jaw-pinch error — coupon check at a 22.09 printed bore came out snug, confirming ~22.0 actual"
- bearing_bore 8.0 catalog
- bearing_w 7.0 catalog
- bolt_shank_d 8.0 measured
- axle_len 50 catalog
- bore_d 22.1 design, note: "608 slip/press fit; coupon printed bore measured 22.09 - bearing snug, holds upside down; confirmed as printed"
- coupon_bore_measured 22.09 world measured, note: "user measured the coupon's printed bearing seat: 22.09 mm, 'goes in, pretty snug; holds upside down'"
- lip_id 20.9 design
- lip_h 1.5 design
- lip_flare 0.5 design
- lip_ramp_h 2.4 design
- lip_segments 3 design count
- thrust_od 15.0 design
- thrust_id 8.6 design
- thrust_t 2.0 design
- edge_chamfer 1.5 design

Criteria: c1 check description updated: "done: coupon bore printed at 22.09 mm; bearing goes in snug and holds upside down". c2 unchanged (tab test not reported — keep as the check that matters; description stays). Others unchanged.

Manual step 1: add "(done — your coupon: seat 22.09 mm, snug, holds upside down)". Step 3: add "the coupon fit is snug — press straight, steadily; it only goes 7.5 mm deep".

Note: mention coupon validated.

Everything else identical. Write it out.

reasoning_details.text:
The user printed the coupon and reports: "22.09 mm seat: goes in, pretty snug; holds upside down."

Interesting — the coupon had a Ø22.1 bore, and they measured the bearing seat as 22.09 mm (probably they measured the printed bore with calipers: it came out 22.09, very close to nominal 22.1). The bearing "goes in, pretty snug; holds upside down" — meaning the bearing fits with a light press fit and even stays put when inverted. That's actually a good outcome for the wheel: the bore is a snug slip/light-press fit.

What does this tell me for the final design?

1. The printed bore at 22.1 nominal comes out at ~22.09 actual — essentially on-size. The bearing fits snugly and holds upside down. For the wheel design, the bore 22.1 gives a light press/ snug fit — the bearings will be nicely retained radially, and the snap lips retain axially. 

2. They didn't mention the lip tab test explicitly ("press the bearing past the lip tab — flexes and snaps back without cracking") — they only mention the seat. Hmm, the report says "22.09 mm seat: goes in, pretty snug; holds upside down." That's the only line. They didn't say whether the tab test worked or the bolt slide test. Since they only reported the seat, I'll assume the rest was fine or at least not alarming. The snug hold upside down is good news — retention is better than expected.

Should I change anything?

Option A: Keep bore_d at 22.1 — validated by the coupon. The bearing holds upside down, which means the light press fit works. In the wheel, both bearings get additional axial retention from the snap lips, and radial retention from the bore.
